record_identity.title: WebinarTV reportedly recorded Zoom meetings and turned them into AI podcasts

source_records.deployment_context: WebinarTV reportedly scanned for publicly discoverable Zoom webinar links, captured sessions, republished recordings and generated AI podcasts from captured content.
source_records.evidence_status_basis: The AIAAIC Repository registry entry records the occurrence, but the entry is not treated as final verification of all underlying claims.
source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used as a secondary incident-registry cross-reference and recurrence signal; factual particulars are anchored more strongly in the underlying 404 Media reporting.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct public review of the AIAAIC repository listing and underlying reporting.
limitations: AIAAIC is a secondary incident registry.
The registry listing alone does not establish every factual detail of each captured webinar.
Legal recording and privacy requirements vary by jurisdiction and context.

source_records.relevance_note: Registry corroboration for the same participant-authority mechanism, extending the issue beyond invited meeting assistants to third-party capture based on technical discoverability or access to a shared interaction.
source_records.source_context: AIAAIC lists WebinarTV as incident 2268. The underlying reporting describes a system that used discoverable Zoom webinar links to access and record sessions, including contexts whose hosts or participants regarded them as private or confidential, and then republished or transformed captured material into AI-generated podcasts.

source_records.deployment_context: Third-party access to Zoom webinar links, recording of sessions and downstream publication or AI transformation of captured material.
source_records.evidence_status_basis: The reviewed independent reporting from 404 Media establishes the occurrence to the extent reported; it does not adjudicate disputed underlying claims.
source_records.interpretive_reliance: Relied upon for the reported scanning, capture, lack-of-permission examples and downstream AI-podcast transformation. VIGIL separately abstracts the failure as participant-specific authority not being independently established.
source_records.model_or_algorithm: automated meeting capture and AI-generated podcast production; exact model stack not publicly established

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct public web review of the 404 Media investigation.
limitations: The investigation does not expose WebinarTV's complete technical stack or every capture pathway.
The legal status of a particular recording depends on jurisdiction and factual context.
VIGIL relies on the authority-boundary mechanism rather than making a universal legal conclusion about all webinars.

source_records.relevance_note: Primary journalistic evidence that mere technical discoverability or access to a webinar link can be operationally treated as sufficient authority to capture and process contributions of other participants, even where those participants did not separately authorise the capture.
source_records.source_context: 404 Media reported that WebinarTV scanned the internet for Zoom links, recorded calls without organisers' or participants' permission in reported cases, and transformed some recordings into AI-generated podcasts. WebinarTV claimed a corpus exceeding 200,000 webinars.
